propositions: Observed ticket lifecycle shows p50 lead time 0.48 days and p50 cycle time 1.52 hours across 2,105 closed work tickets over 68-day window (Q2–Q3 2026), but neither throughput nor cycle speed establishes sustainable flow or quality without defect and detection-stage data.

Plan-review adoption rose from 29.2% (Q2, review-before-claim) to 79.5% (Q3), with first-pass rate 49.0% and p90 retry attempts 8, yet 116,560 LLM calls per 114 accepted completions indicates process maturation rather than efficiency.

Completion first-pass rate is 72.3% (722/998); Testing-section headings correlate with 79.7% first-pass versus 68.6% without, and file-impact declarations with 74.2% versus 67.6%, but causality and confounders remain unmeasured.

Current bugs (648) lack detected_by metadata except 7 records (1.1% adoption), preventing calculation of true escape rate or detection-stage efficiency; caused_by links are advisory and demonstrably noisy (author-supplied, larger diffs bias blame attribution), not ground truth.

Commit process governance adoption reached ~100% by August (ticket trailer 90.4%, DCO 82.9%, Change-Id 99.3%); source-change median churn improved Q2→Q3 (111.5→95 lines), test co-change increased (84.5→160.5 lines), and test-to-source LOC ratio is 2.09×, supporting process maturation but not proven quality improvement.

Code-health analysis identifies 35 modules at or above 720 LOC (4 near hard 800-LOC cap), 4.09% duplication, 0.231 refactor-to-addition ratio, and same-file retouch within 24h in 47.7% of pairs, signaling debt pressure and hotspots; caused_by-linked sources show larger diffs (median 912 vs 256 lines) and lower initial plan PASS (30.3% vs 49.5%), but authorship concentration (92.4% top operator/bot) precludes independent human-review validation.
